transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-18 16:00 PDT; Duration: ~45 minutes; Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Riya (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO - Stellarus), Carlos (ML Eng), Lina (Product)

Summary: quick scoping for a 4-week POC to validate open-models for domain-aware extraction and summarization across English/Spanish. Primary success criteria: extraction F1 >= 0.85 on labeled set, latency p50 < 300ms for single-turn summarization, cost target < $0.02/request at expected volume. Discussed model shortlist, hardware options (A100 vs H100), quantization/latency tradeoffs, and benchmark plan.

Topics: POC goals; dataset & evaluation; model shortlist and quality tradeoffs; infra & benchmark plan; timelines and deliverables.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, uh, quick intros. I'm Jordan from Redwood, account lead.
00:10 Maya: Maya here, CTO at Stellarus. Thanks for fitting us in.
00:14 Carlos: Carlos, ML engineer, I'll be hands on for the evals.
00:18 Lina: Lina, product, focusing on business metrics and timelines.
00:22 Riya: Riya, solutions eng at Redwood, I'll own the benchmark and infra conversation.

00:35 Jordan: Goal for today is to scope a POC around open models — we heard you want open-models for licensing and reproducibility. Confirming it's a 4-week pilot to validate quality and perf on your document extraction slash summarization workflows?
00:50 Maya: Yeah that's right. Two core flows: 1) structured extraction from regulatory docs in English/Spanish; 2) multi-paragraph summarization for internal knowledge. Both need decent multilingual performance. Not looking to ship in prod until we can hit accuracy and cost targets.
01:05 Carlos: quick question — our labeled set is about 3k annotated fields for extraction, and summarization testset ~500 docs average 800 tokens. Throughput target is approx 500 requests per hour during business hours, burst to 2k. Latency target is p50 under 300ms for short summaries (~200 tokens) and p95 under 1.2s. Does that map to the typical POC scope you do?
01:30 Riya: that's totally reasonable. We'll size the baseline infra but quick note — those latency numbers push toward larger GPUs or optimized quantization. For open models we typically test a small shortlist and compare both accuracy and tokens/sec.
01:44 Jordan: on success criteria can you confirm the business threshold? Lina?
01:48 Lina: We want extraction F1 >= 0.85 on the labeled set and summary usefulness score (internal rubric) average >= 4/5. Cost target is rough: under $0.02 per request at your expected profile — mainly because we'll be doing many summarizations daily.
02:05 Jordan: great. Ok Riya, do you want to walk through the model shortlist you recommend?
02:12 Riya: sure. For open models we've seen these reasonable tradeoffs — note these are initial suggestions, we'll run benchmarks. Candidate list: Llama-2-13B-instruct (cheaper, decent for instruction), Llama-2-70B (higher quality, heavy), Mixtral-8x7B (aka mixtral, good few-shot), Mistral-7B-Instruct (fast, strong on reasoning tasks), Falcon-40B-Instruct (strong generative quality). We'll also consider 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants.
02:44 Carlos: a couple clarifying points — we need Spanish specifically, some models like Llama variants are okay but we've seen dropoff on legal Spanish. Do you have any pre-eval benchmarks on Spanish for these models?
02:58 Riya: yes, we have existing perf profiles but language gaps happen. That's why the POC will include a multi-lingual slice. Preliminary notes: Mixtral and Mistral family tend to be surprisingly good on Romance languages; Llama-70B generally strong but more expensive. Falcon's newer weights have good generative fluency but can hallucinate on extraction tasks unless you tune prompts and use few-shot.
03:18 Maya: interesting, so practically how do we run the benchmark? We'd prefer Redwood to host runs to mirror production. Also what GPU types will you use? H100 vs A100?
03:28 Riya: we can run on both. For low-latency targets we'll prioritize H100-backed instances for the 70B class to get better perf; 13B and 7B classes run well on A100 with 8-bit/4-bit quantization and specialized kernels. We'll provide throughput/latency/cost matrix per model/instance config.
03:45 Jordan: for cost estimates we'll include both hosted and an estimate if you later choose dedicated capacity. For the POC you probably want Redwood-hosted so we can iterate fast.
03:53 Lina: yeah hosted is fine for evaluation. Security wise, we need SOC2, SSO, and logs. Jordan you said you'd share docs?
04:01 Jordan: yes action item — I'll send SOC2 report, architecture, and data handling info after the call.
04:07 Carlos: about evaluation metrics — for extraction we'll use F1 on our gold labels, for summarization we have a human rubric and ROUGE/Lexical metrics but human quality matters more. We'll provide an evaluation script.
04:22 Riya: perfect. Our benchmark plan will run: precision/recall on extraction, summary usefulness (human) + automatic proxies, latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per request. We'll also test prompt engineering (zero-shot vs 3-shot) and caching impacts — e.g., prefix/KV-cache for repeated docs.
04:41 Maya: what's the timeline? We want results before end of July ideally.
04:45 Jordan: timeline we proposed — this week 6/18 scoping, by 6/23 you send samples & eval script, 6/30 - 7/04 Redwood runs benchmarks, 7/08 follow-up to review results. That fits your end-of-July constraint.
04:59 Lina: sounds good. Also curious about hallucinations on extraction — is there an approach to reduce?
05:06 Riya: yes — structured prompts, few-shot anchors, using constrained generation (extractive templates), and post-processing with regex checks. Another lever is model size: bigger models often hallucinate less but cost more. Also we can try reranking pipelines or hybrid approach: smaller model for candidate extraction + larger for verification.
05:27 Carlos: oh that hybrid idea could be useful to keep costs down. Could Redwood orchestrate multi-model pipelines in the POC?
05:34 Riya: absolutely, we can set up a pipeline so requests route by policy — e.g., candidate generation on Mixtral-8x7B, verify on Llama-2-70B only for low-confidence cases. We'll measure the unit economics for that pattern.
05:46 Maya: network constraints — we're behind a corporate proxy and require IP allowlist. For a hosted POC, what's the typical setup?
05:54 Jordan: we support IP allowlisting and can do a VPN/VPC peering setup for Private deployments later, but for POC we'll use token-based auth and IP allowlist. I'll include specifics in the security pack.
06:05 Carlos: on evaluation size — should we include both full-doc and chunked contexts? Some of our regulatory docs are 6k tokens.
06:13 Riya: yes include both. We'll test chunked + retrieval augmentation and long-context model performance where available. We expect chunking+ranked retrieval to be cost-effective.
06:24 Lina: any gotchas around quantization for Spanish legal language?
06:28 Riya: sometimes quantization degrades nuanced language understanding, especially for out-of-distribution domain text. We'll parallel test FP16/Half precision as baseline and 4-bit/8-bit quantized runs to see the delta. We'll surface per-task quality drop.
06:42 Maya: ok last bit — stakeholders, who wants the benchmark report?
06:46 Lina: myself and Maya and Carlos — and our security lead for the docs.
06:51 Jordan: great. We'll circulate notes and action items. Riya, wrap next steps?
06:56 Riya: we'll produce a benchmark plan by Friday 6/20, Jordan will send security pack by tomorrow 6/19, Stellarus to send samples by 6/23, Redwood runs a first-pass benchmark week of 6/30 and we'll recon on 7/08 to decide production approach.
07:13 Maya: thanks all.
07:15 Jordan: thanks everyone, end call.

Post-call notes: Redwood recommended initial shortlist: Mixtral-8x7B (cost-efficient, good multi-lingual), Mistral-7B-Instruct (fast), Llama-2-13B-instruct (baseline), Llama-2-70B (quality/upper bound), Falcon-40B-Instruct (generative). Plan to test quantized variants and hybrid orchestration. POC success gating hinges on extraction F1 and latency/cost thresholds.
